dedupe_keys.name: post disaster recovery modelling of school infrastructure opabola and galasso matlab

description: This MATLAB code implements a method for estimating how quickly education services recover after a disaster, published by Eyitayo Opabola and Carmine Galasso in Nature Communications (January 2024) to test disaster management policies for schools in low- and lower-middle-income countries. Three folders reproduce the paper's case studies on a hypothetical earthquake hitting a testbed of school buildings in Central Sulawesi, Indonesia. The first simulates short-term functionality recovery through temporary learning centres, depending on whether early response financing is in place; the second runs Monte Carlo critical-path analysis with PERT task durations to give reconstruction time distributions under different project management types; the third ranks schools with the TOPSIS multicriteria method to account for socio-political factors. The paper reports that early financing speeds education recovery about threefold and community-managed reconstruction finishes three to five times faster than agency-managed projects. Coverage: an 80-building testbed in Central Sulawesi, with school locations removed from the uploaded files. Access: GitHub repository and Zenodo archive v2.0 (4 November 2023), with a README per folder describing inputs. Licence: MIT; free. Caveats: sample hazard inputs are included but the underlying hazard analysis and stakeholder-derived factors come from the paper. Simulation uses are recovery and continuity modelling for school portfolios in resilience studies. Related records: the Central Sulawesi school buildings inventory.
inputs: School building inventory (students, code level, storeys, typology)
Seismic intensity samples (PGA and spectral acceleration at 0.2 s)
Availability of anticipatory funds for temporary learning centres
Repair task sequences with PERT duration parameters
name: Post-disaster recovery modelling of school infrastructure (Opabola and Galasso, MATLAB)
outputs: Short-term functionality recovery trajectories with temporary learning centres
TOPSIS ranking of schools for recovery priority
provider: Eyitayo Opabola and Carmine Galasso (University College London), code on GitHub and Zenodo
